ogTitle: Where to Stay in Ping Riverside, Chiang Mai
ogDesc: The best hotels in Ping Riverside by budget.
intro: The Ping riverside feels different from the Old City: water views, big trees, and quiet, especially along Charoenrat Road near Wat Ket, which is lined with old buildings, cafes, and river-facing restaurants. Most hotels sit on both banks. The Charoenrat side is the quieter boutique zone, while the Charoen Prathet side is closer to the Night Bazaar. The whole area is only a 5-10 minute drive from Tha Phae Gate and the Old City, so it suits travellers who want riverside calm but still easy access into town.

blocks.html: Short answer: The Ping River stretch along Charoenrat Road, Wat Ket, and Nawarat Bridge is Chiang Mai's calm riverside neighbourhood, running from small boutiques up to upscale resorts. You get riverside walks, water-facing restaurants, and cafes in old shophouses, with the Night Bazaar and Old City just a short drive away. Rates start around ฿1,400 and climb into five figures for a river-view suite.

items.name: At Pingnakorn Riverside
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Value · riverside on the Wat Ket side · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 4-star hotel on Charoenrat Road on the Wat Ket side, opened in 2017 and renovated in 2024. Rooms are fairly large and clean, with an outdoor pool and a garden along the Ping River. Reviews praise the breakfast and the quiet riverside location, and you can walk the river path to the cafes and restaurants around Wat Ket. It's the best value pick in the area if you want a spacious room with a garden view.

items.name: Sala Lanna Chiang Mai
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Small boutique · rooftop bar · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 15-room boutique hotel at 49 Charoenrat Road, right on the river on the Wat Ket bank. Its highlight is a 360-degree rooftop bar that's lovely at sunset, plus the riverside Wanlamun Rim Nam restaurant. The design blends Lanna and modern touches, and there's a rooftop pool. A good match for couples or anyone who prefers a small, private-feeling stay, and it's walkable to the Night Bazaar.

items.name: Cross Chiang Mai Riverside
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Upscale boutique · old tamarind trees · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 29-room, 5-star resort at 369/1 Charoenrat Road on the Wat Ket bank, set along the Ping River among century-old tamarind trees and green gardens. Rooms are contemporary, with a pool and a spa (formerly branded X2 Chiang Mai Riverside). It suits travellers who want an upscale resort that isn't too big, with a focus on calm and private riverside space.

items.name: Ping Nakara Boutique Hotel & Spa
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Colonial style · riverside spa · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 19-room boutique hotel in early-1900s colonial style at 135/9 Charoen Prathet Road, on the side closer to the Night Bazaar. The fretwork woodwork and decor are what guests mention most, and there's the riverside Nakara Spa and a rooftop terrace. It's about a 5-minute walk to the Night Bazaar, ideal for travellers who like a design-led stay with a period atmosphere.

items.name: RatiLanna Riverside Spa Resort
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Larger resort · spa and riverside pool · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 97-room, 5-star resort on Charoen Prathet Road along the Ping River, with spacious Lanna-style rooms, a riverside pool, a spa, and a river-facing restaurant. It's within walking distance of the Night Bazaar. Being larger than the boutiques in this area, it works well for families or anyone who wants full facilities in one place along with a river view.

items.name: Anantara Chiang Mai Resort
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Riverside luxury · minimalist design · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A luxury resort on the Ping River at 123 Charoen Prathet Road, with clean modern-minimalist design, a riverside pool, a spa, and a river-facing restaurant that guests rate highly, especially the afternoon tea in the old colonial house. It's close to the Night Bazaar and Nawarat Bridge, suited to travellers who want high-end service and a riverside setting in the centre of town.

items.name: 137 Pillars House
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Top-tier luxury · all-suite · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: An all-suite hotel on a quiet lane near Wat Ket, close to Charoenrat Road. The property pairs a historic teak house with contemporary wings, and every room is a spacious suite with a private balcony. There's a pool, a spa, and a place in the MICHELIN Guide. It's the priciest option in the area, best for a special occasion or for travellers who want the hotel itself to be the destination.

faq.q: Is it hard to reach the Old City and Night Bazaar from the Ping riverside?
faq.a: Not at all. The whole area is just a 5-10 minute drive from Tha Phae Gate and the Old City. Hotels on the Charoen Prathet side like RatiLanna, Ping Nakara, and Anantara are within walking distance of the Night Bazaar, while the Charoenrat side near Wat Ket is a bit quieter, but a taxi or Grab into town is easy and cheap.

faq.q: What's the difference between the Charoenrat side and the Charoen Prathet side?
faq.a: The Charoenrat side (Wat Ket) is the quieter boutique zone, with old buildings, cafes, and riverside restaurants to stroll between, good for a calm atmosphere. The Charoen Prathet side is closer to the Night Bazaar and street food, handy for evening shopping. Both sit on the Ping River, so choose based on whether you want quiet or convenience.

faq.q: Who is the Ping riverside good for, and who should skip it?
faq.a: It suits couples, families, and anyone who wants river views and a calm setting, with options from value boutiques to luxury resorts. If you'd rather stay inside the Old City to walk between temples and markets, or be near the Nimman cafe scene, the Old City or Nimman may fit better, since out here you mostly rely on a car to get in and out.
